Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Breathing difficulty after wasp sting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient was stung by a wasp while gardening 15 minutes ago.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: 15 min ago stung by wasp while gardening

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Following the wasp sting, the patient developed shallow breathing.
Following the wasp sting, the patient developed chest tightness.
Following the wasp sting, the patient developed lip tingling without swelling.
Following the wasp sting, the patient developed a blotchy rash.
This is the first episode of such a reaction.

Medications.content: Patient keeps over-the-counter antihistamines for aerosinusitis.
Medications.source_text: Meds: keeps OTC antihistamines for aerosinusitis

Medications.content: Patient is on no regular prescription medications.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient's wife is present and can call an ambulance.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: SH: Wife present, can call ambulance

Assessment.content: Suspected anaphylactic reaction status post wasp sting with respiratory symptoms, lip tingling, and cutaneous rash.
Assessment.source_text: Suspected anaphylactic reaction s/p wasp sting – resp Sx, lip tingling, cutaneous rash

Plan_of_Care.content: Instruct wife to call ambulance immediately.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Instruct wife to call ambulance immediately

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient to take oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Take oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS

Plan_of_Care.content: Urgent emergency department evaluation for airway support, epinephrine, and monitoring.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Urgent ED eval for airway support, epinephrine, monitoring

Plan_of_Care.content: Educate patient on potential rapid progression of anaphylaxis.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Educate on potential rapid progression of anaphylaxis
